messages:
Sam Baker: Ran an NSYS capture on the repro (small batch, 4 GPUs). Seeing a recurring ~2.5ms host-side gap every ~120ms right at what looks like epoch boundaries. Memcpy H2D spikes and kernels serialize.
Maria Chen: can you paste the capture command and a tiny waterfall snippet?
Sam Baker: command I used:
```
nsys profile --output trace_epoch --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none --duration=120s 
python run_repro.py --batch 1 --seq 2048
```
Sam Baker: uploaded trace file -> trace_epoch.qdrep. Timeline: stream 2 shows clumped cudaMemcpyAsync (H2D) that coincide with stream 0 kernels stalling. CPU shows short hostspin then pthread wakeups.
Kai Patel: hmm. Any KV-cache ops at the epoch boundary? eviction/prefetch maybe?
Sam Baker: yes — our kvcache prefetch runs a full-keyset rehydrate every epoch to warm the cache. It triggers multiple H2D memcpy batches at once.
Devin O'Neill: That matches. Bulk prefetch currently allocates regular host buffers (not pinned) then issues cudaMemcpyAsync on a stream that ends up synchronizing with default stream -> driver inserts staging copies which can behave synchronously.
Maria Chen: can you show the nsight waterfall text around one event? just 8-12 lines.
Sam Baker: pasted minimal waterfall (nsys text view):
```
[120.032s] cudaMemcpyAsync H2D size=8MB stream=2 duration=1.8ms
[120.035s] kernel_X stream=0 enqueue timestamp
[120.036s] kernel_X start 120.038s  <-- delayed until memcpy completes
[120.038s] cudaMemcpyAsync H2D size=9MB stream=2 duration=2.1ms
[120.041s] pthread wakeup main_thread
```
Kai Patel: kernels on stream0 wait because those H2D memcpys are effectively synchronizing device work (implicit ordering or default-stream interactions). If prefetch uses nonblocking streams but host memory isn't pinned, there are still driver-side stalls.
Devin O'Neill: also saw small CPU scheduling gaps (~1-3ms) when host thread is doing allocation+memcpy work. That bumps latency for our micro-batches.
Maria Chen: experiments planned?
Sam Baker: experiments I ran so far:
- switched prefetch to cudaHostAlloc (pinned) + cudaMemcpyAsync on a dedicated non-default stream -> removed the ~2.5ms stall in the repro.
- moved prefetch work to a lower-priority stream and used cudaStreamWaitEvent to control ordering -> reduced kernel delays.
- staggered rehydrate keys (spread across ticks) instead of bulk epoch flush -> smoothed memcpy spikes.
Kai Patel: two levers for immediate fix: 1) make kvcache prefetch use pinned buffers + dedicated streams, 2) update the batching heuristic to distribute epoch rehydrates across small time windows.
Maria Chen: also add a gate so prefetch only runs when GPU util < 20% to avoid stomping active workloads.
Sam Baker: numbers from the repro: median pipeline latency dropped from ~9.4ms -> ~7.1ms, p95 from ~18.9ms -> ~12.3ms after pinned+stream changes. CPU sys% decreased too.
Devin O'Neill: note: some driver-level cross-stream fences still caused serialization on a couple kernels. We should audit use of default stream and any implicit memcpy-synchronizing APIs.
Maria Chen: PR plan:
- kvcache: allocate a small pinned-buffer pool + async copy path (Sam)
- runtime: implement prefetch spread heuristic + GPU-util gating (Kai)
- infra: add a small NSYS smoke test that captures an epoch boundary trace in CI (Devin)
Sam Baker: will open the PRs and attach before/after traces. Tagging @devops for pinned-mem quota on CI.
trace-bot: uploaded artifacts: s3://redwood-traces/trace_epoch_before.qdrep, s3://redwood-traces/trace_epoch_after.qdrep
Maria Chen: thanks — once PRs land, let's validate across 8/16 GPU configs. I'll mark action items and close thread after cross-config results.
Kai Patel: reminder: document the heuristic in runtime docs (what counts as an epoch, tunable window) so on-call can adjust thresholds.
Sam Baker: ack, will add notes in the PR. :thumbsup:
